description: Manage Snowflake tables under /api/v2/databases/{database}/schemas/{schema}/tables. Operations: list (like, startsWith, showLimit 1-10000, fromName, history, deep), create (body Table with name, for example columns, constraints, cluster_by, kind, comment; createMode, copyGrants), create_as_select (required query parameter query, the SELECT; body TableAsSelect with name, optional columns and cluster_by; tables:as-select), create_using_template (required query parameter query; optional body with name; tables:using-template), get, create_or_alter (PUT body Table), delete (ifExists), clone (name is the source; body TableClone with name and optional point_of_time; createMode, copyGrants, targetDatabase, targetSchema), create_like (name is the source; body with the new name; createMode, copyGrants), undrop, suspend_recluster and resume_recluster (ifExists), swap_with (required targetName; ifExists, targetDatabase, targetSchema), set_tags, unset_tags (tags; ifExists), get_tags (withLineage) and fetch_result (result_handler, page). Vendor-deprecated underscore paths stay on request. Vendor RBAC alone decides. Returns job_id/status queued.
embedding_description: Create, alter, clone, copy the structure of, swap, undrop and drop Snowflake tables through the Table REST API, including create-as-select from a query and create from a schema-detection template, pausing or resuming automatic clustering, and tagging. Use for table lifecycle in a database schema; vendor role grants decide every write and delete.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Queued dispatch: job_id and status. Completion: family, operation, method, status (HTTP), headers, body (Table objects with columns, constraints and clustering, the vendor's status message, tags or a SuccessAcceptedResponse), body_encoding, correlation_id, error_code for 4xx/5xx, and pagination: next_from_name when a list page filled showLimit, Link relations, location and result_handler for 202 responses.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This operation may have changed vendor state. Queued means the job was accepted, not that Snowflake completed the operation. Report the HTTP status, error_code and body faithfully. Report deletes, renames and swaps from the vendor status, never from job completion alone.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Manage Snowflake tables with the registered role's grants.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: snowflake.invalid_params is raised before any vendor call when the operation, identifiers, query parameter names, types or ranges (boolean ifExists, copyGrants, history and deep; showLimit 1-10000), a missing required query (query for create_as_select and create_using_template, targetName for swap_with), createMode or required body members (name for create, create_or_alter and clone) do not match the documented vendor shape. Vendor HTTP errors are completion data with status, body and error_code: auth_failed (401), permission_denied (403), object_not_found (404), timeout (408), conflict (409), rate_limited (429), api_error otherwise. snowflake.api_error without a status is a transport or configuration failure.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Read the vendor status and body before retrying. A 403 means the registered role lacks the grant: grant it in Snowflake, the plugin adds no gate of its own. Double-quote identifiers that contain other characters. For a 202, call the same verb with operation fetch_result and the pagination.result_handler. Never silently retry a mutation after a transport error: read the object first.
